chunks: We were told by Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid, may Allah grant him mercy, that he said: We were told by Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Khattab, from Ali ibn Asbat, from Ahmad ibn Umar al-Hallal, from Ali ibn Suwayd al-Madeeni, from Abu al-Hasan Musa (peace be upon him), who said:

I asked him about the wonder (or vanity) that invalidates deeds, he said: The wonder has ranks: among them is that evil deeds are beautified for the servant, so he sees them as good, admires them, and assumes that he is doing good; and among them is that the servant believes in his Lord, so he considers himself performing a favor upon Allah, Blessed and Exalted is He, whereas Allah, Exalted is He, is the One who granted him the favor.

key_terms.الْعَجَب: Vanity or self-admiration; a spiritual state that invalidates deeds
key_terms.فِيهِ الْمَنُّ: Considering it a favor/grace bestowed upon God
key_terms.يُفْسِدُ الْعَمَلَ: To invalidate or spoil the deed

ai.seo_question: What is al-'ajab and how does it invalidate good deeds according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In *Mani al-Akhbar*, Shaykh al-Saduq records Imam Musa al-Kazim (AS) defining 'al-'ajab' not merely as pride, but as a subtle spiritual blindness that corrupts the sincerity of worship. This phenomenon manifests either by distorting one's perception of their own actions, making evil appear good, or by the servant attributing their faith to their own merit rather than God's grace, thereby introducing a subtle form of self-reliance (*istighna*) into devotion.

en.basel-kadem: 1.	We were told by Muhammed bin Hasan bin Ahmad bin Waleed, may Allah grant him mercy, that he said: We were told by Muhammed bin Hasan al-Saffar, from Muhammed bin Hussain bin Abi’l-Khattab, from Ali bin Asbat, from Ahmad bin Umar al-Hallal, from Ali bin Suwayd al-Madeeni, from Abu’l-Hasan, Musa, peace be upon him, that he said:

I asked him about the veils which invalidate deeds. He said: The veils are (different) ranks: among them is what beautifies for a servant his evil deed, by which he sees it as good, admires it and assumes that he is doing good; and among them is that a servant believes in his Lord, by which he (assumes that he) performs a favor upon Allah, Blessed and Exalted is He, whereas Allah, Exalted is He, is the One who granted him a favor.
